core.title: Out-of-band swap tests assert the destination id
core.given: A test case whose body mentions the out-of-band swap construct, e.g. asserting an out-of-band swap is present in a response
core.when: the test case is present in the suite (new, changed or existing)
core.then: The same test case MUST also assert the destination `id` the out-of-band element will be matched against.
prefer: Assert the destination, not just the mechanism: assert the out-of-band swap construct is present (the server's half only), then assert the destination id is present (the half that must match the page).
Any id-reaching assertion works; no specific matcher is required.
Bind the runtime-artefact assertion back to the declaration it came from: the id the page declares.
avoid: Half assertions: checking that the out-of-band swap construct appears and stopping — proves only the server's half, not the destination a refactor of the served page breaks.
An id assertion unrelated to the out-of-band element's destination, just to satisfy the check.
unless: The test case never mentions the out-of-band swap construct (out of scope).
core.why: The hypermedia client silently drops an out-of-band element whose id matches nothing in the document (no error, no warning, no swap); the id must be in the response AND the document. The paired coder-side rule makes the server emit an id; only this rule makes a test prove it is the id the page will match.
evidence: Every test case whose body mentions the out-of-band swap construct contains at least one id-reaching assertion.
The rule's check reports no findings across the test suite.
Reviewer note: whether the id actually EXISTS in the served document is a runtime fact no static check can see; static compliance only proves the test asserts an id.
verification: Suite-wide static check over test cases: every test case whose body mentions the out-of-band swap construct (any mention, not only assertions) is inspected, whether or not it changed; test cases that never mention the construct are not inspected.

The check flags a test case whose body mentions the out-of-band swap construct but contains no assertion reaching an id; which assertion forms count as id-reaching is stack idiom taken from the profile, and any id-reaching assertion satisfies the rule — no specific matcher is required.
Limitation: existence of the id in the served document is a runtime fact outside the static check; static compliance only proves the test asserts an id.
Task-term match is a non-gating hint only; the rule applies to qualifying test cases regardless of task wording.
Severity 3; disposition strict: the check fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: test case body mentions the out-of-band swap construct
out-of-band swap mention without an id-reaching assertion

fires: A test case asserts the response contains the out-of-band swap construct and has no assertion reaching the destination id.
An existing, unchanged test case only checks that the out-of-band swap construct is present and is scanned by the suite check.
A test case body mentions the out-of-band swap construct anywhere (e.g. in a fixture string, comment or helper argument, not as an assertion) and contains no id-reaching assertion.
doesNotFire: A test case that never mentions the out-of-band swap construct.
A test case mentioning the out-of-band swap construct that also has any id-reaching assertion (any form the stack's profile recognises; no specific matcher is required).
Production boundary or presentation code that emits the out-of-band element (covered by the paired coder-side rule, not this one).

profileRequirements.meaning: The declarative markup construct that marks an element for an out-of-band swap into the document; the rule's trigger, scope test and check all scan test-case bodies for any mention of it (assertion or not).
The stack's test-assertion forms that count as reaching a specific element id; any one of them satisfies the rule and no specific matcher is required.
profileRequirements.bunValue: an `id=` inside an expected string, a `getElementById` call, a `querySelector('#…')`, or a `toHaveAttribute('id'…`)

proposedKeys.meaning: The declarative markup construct that marks an element for an out-of-band swap into the document; test bodies mention it in any form when an out-of-band swap is involved.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group covers request constructs (destructive_request, mutation_requests) and gates (confirmation_gate, prompt_gate), plus which artifact kinds count as markup (markup_kinds), but has no key for the out-of-band swap construct itself.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's test-assertion forms that count as asserting a specific element id (the id-reaching forms this rule accepts).
proposedKeys.bunValue: an `id=` inside an expected string, a `getElementById` call, a `querySelector('#…')`, or a `toHaveAttribute('id'…`)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key describes test-assertion idioms; the idiom group covers only source-side constructs (handlers, imports, naming, markup request/gate constructs).

neutralityNotes: The rule is inherently hypermedia-family: it presupposes a client that retargets response elements into the document by id (an out-of-band swap). Stacks without such a construct cannot realize it, which is why the construct itself is a profile key (idiom.oob_swap_construct, proposed) rather than core text. Bun's single 'test' file kind was rendered as the three test roles (unit/acceptance/e2e) with unchanged scope. The detector's concrete id-reaching matcher list travels as profile data (idiom.id_reaching_assertions, proposed), not as core text, since the forms are test-library-specific while the acceptance rule (any id-reaching assertion, no specific matcher) is neutral. The paired coder-side rule is referenced generically because its Bun rule id is realization-specific. Nothing else resisted neutralization.
